title: False positives grow with the number of tests
caption: Each test has a 5% false-positive chance, but the chance of at least one among n independent tests is 1 − 0.95ⁿ. For 20 tests that is 0.64: more likely than not, so a lone "significant" result among many is weak evidence.
alt: Probability of at least one false positive against the number of tests, rising from 0.05 at one test to 0.64 at twenty and towards 1.
description: P(at least one) = 1 − (1 − α)^n with α = 0.05.
Corrections such as Bonferroni (α/n per test) restore the overall rate.
